data.body:
Final AC verified: the full live `completion-verifier` standing eval PASSES on main with the fix.

Run: fresh throwaway worktree at origin/main tip 94df7a8db5 (contains 08918c7314 'Root eval agent runs at their case fixtures', Gerrit 1608, merged), model bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8, REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION=us-east-1, entry point `rebar.llm.evals.eval.run_eval('completion-verifier')` — the same call the prompt-eval live CI job makes, with NO max_cases cap so the whole 11-case dataset ran.

Result — full 11 cases x 3 epochs, no reduction:
  passed=True  coverage=1.0  epoch_pass=[True, True, True]  gate=at_least(2)  epochs=3
JUnit: 69 testcases, 0 failures.

This is the direct inverse of the failure recorded in the ticket Evidence section (coverage 1.0 but epoch_pass [False, False, False]). The cases that previously failed were the targeted COMPLETE ones (CV-complete-feature / CV-complete-bugfix / CV-complete-refactor) — they searched the eval checkout, could not see fixture files such as src/cli.py or app/profile.py, and so wrongly returned FAIL; the operator-attested cases, which need no fixture code, passed even before the fix. All three complete cases now pass in all three epochs, which is what demonstrates the agent's filesystem tools are rooted at each disposable case fixture rather than the checkout.

A 2-case pilot run first (as a cost probe) also passed 3/3 at coverage 1.0. Cost: 33 case-runs, 164 requests, 1,463,801 input / 25,378 output tokens, est. $1.03 — comfortably inside budget, so the full 3-epoch gate was run as the AC demands rather than a subset.

All four acceptance criteria are now met; closing.
